tasks.learning: Trace how a raw command-line string becomes a typed option value passed to a Click callback. Read the current code and describe source precedence, defaults, environment variables, nargs/multiple conversion, and the relevant file:symbol pointers. Explain existing behavior only; do not change code, propose fixes, inspect git history, or browse the web.
tasks.prompt: Fix string values in default_map for multi-value parameters. For example, an integer option with nargs=2 and default_map={'point': '3 4'} should receive (3, 4), rather than treating the string as characters or raising a conversion error. Explicit tuple types should work too. Use the parameter type's environment-value splitting semantics, preserve already-structured tuple/list defaults, and preserve command-line precedence over default_map. Add appropriate tests and document the behavior.

tasks.learning: Explain how Click's current CliRunner.invoke and isolation manage stdin/stdout/stderr, their buffers and stream wrappers, exceptions and exit codes, and restoration after a command finishes. Inspect the implementation and representative existing tests, cite file:symbol pointers, and describe current behavior. Do not modify code, propose fixes, inspect git history, or browse the web.
tasks.prompt: Add an explicit capture mode to CliRunner and fix its default exposure of real file descriptors. CliRunner(capture='sys') must be the default: capture Python-level writes while leaving sys.stdout.fileno() and sys.stderr.fileno() raising io.UnsupportedOperation so code cannot accidentally redirect the host runner. Add capture='fd' on non-Windows platforms to capture direct os.write(1/2), writes through stale stream references or logging handlers, and allow faulthandler.enable(). Keep stdout/stderr separate and include both in Result.output. Restore original streams and descriptors even on exceptions; nested invocations and interaction with pytest's capsys/capfd must work. Reject invalid capture values and reject fd mode on Windows with clear ValueErrors. Preserve existing invocation/exit behavior. Add tests and update the testing documentation.

controls: Same pinned model and medium reasoning in every model phase; no fallback
Fresh exploration evidence shared identically between separate builders; no thinker notes to Mem0
Same tasks, pinned thinker implementation, memory budgets and arm order as Sonnet cohort
Isolated history-free snapshot worktrees and Codex homes; no MCP/global hooks
Tools disabled during memory building; recorded calls must contain no tool use
Prefetched memory only; no live retrieval or post-edit memory updates
Acceptance uses untouched upstream post-fix test module; full suite also run
Coding runs sequential; model cache state not reset
limitations: Two public historical tasks, one run per arm; possible training-data familiarity
Sandbox allows reads outside checkout; prompt rules plus trace audit enforce study boundaries
Different Codex/Claude harnesses and newly generated evidence make cross-model results separate cohorts, not causal model comparisons
Windows-only acceptance case skipped on macOS
Source-session costs reported separately; no dollar estimates
